title.rendered: Do You Want to Get Well?: The Gospel For Today

excerpt.rendered: “Do you want to be healed?” A morning devotional on Jesus’ searching question to a man who had been sick for 38 years.

content.rendered:
He had been sick for thirty-eight years. Longer than most of the people in the crowd around him had been alive. And when Jesus reached him at the Pool of Bethesda, He asked the strangest possible question. “Do you want to be made well?”

The Gospel For Today | Wednesday, September 9, 2026

Today’s Scripture

“When Jesus saw him lying there, and knew that he already had been in that condition a long time, He said to him, ‘Do you want to be made well?'”
John 5:6 (NKJV)

Today’s Message

He had been sick for thirty-eight years. Longer than most of the people in the crowd around him had been alive. He lay on his mat by the Pool of Bethesda, at the Sheep Gate in Jerusalem, one of a great multitude of the sick who waited by the five porticoes hoping for a moment of miraculous stirring of the water. According to the tradition of the day, an angel would occasionally trouble the pool, and the first sick person to step in would be healed. But this man had no one to carry him in. Every time the water stirred, someone else got there first. Thirty-eight years of being not-fast-enough. Then, one Sabbath afternoon, a stranger stopped in front of him. Looked at him. Knew him without a word being exchanged. And asked the strangest possible question. “Do you want to be made well?”

It is a startling question. Of course he wanted to be made well. That is why he was at the pool. That is why he had been at the pool for years. But Jesus does not ask questions He does not intend. He was asking the man to face a question the man may have quietly stopped asking himself. Did he still want it? After thirty-eight years, wanting hurts. Hope hurts. Being disappointed one more time hurts. Sometimes the soul builds a little life around the sickness and forgets how to want what it once wanted. Jesus, in one sentence, opened the door for the man to say yes again. To hope again. To risk again.

The Passion Translation renders it with striking directness: “Jesus recognized him and knew how long he had been crippled. He asked the man, ‘Do you truly long to be healed?'” (John 5:6 TPT). The Amplified Bible Classic Edition adds: “When Jesus noticed him lying there [helpless], knowing that he had already been a long time in that condition, He said to him, Do you want to become well? [Are you really in earnest about getting well?]” (John 5:6 AMPC). Are you really in earnest. Are you still in the fight. Is your heart still where you say it is.

The man does not exactly answer yes. He explains why the healing has not happened. “Sir, I have no man to put me into the pool when the water is stirred up; but while I am coming, another steps down before me.” He explains the obstacle. He names the disappointment. He does not ask for what he wants. He describes why what he wants has not come. And Jesus, without waiting for a better answer, bypasses the pool entirely and speaks the healing directly into the man’s body. “Rise, take up your bed and walk.” Immediately, John writes, the man was made well. Immediately, he took up his bed and walked. The thirty-eight-year wait was over in a sentence.

For Gospelbuzz readers today, Jesus is still asking the question He asked at the pool. Do you want to be made well? Wherever you are reading this from, in Lagos or London or Manila or Nairobi or Sao Paulo, there may be an area of your life where you have been sick for a long time. A wound. A pattern. A brokenness. A fear. A weight you have carried for so long that you have almost stopped hoping for its removal. Jesus is asking the same question He asked the man at Bethesda. Not because He does not know the answer. Because He wants you to face it, and to ask again for what you have almost stopped asking for. The pool is not the point. The healer is the point. And He is standing in front of you today, willing, able, and asking. Do you want to be made well?

Prayer

Father, I acknowledge that Jesus is still asking the healing question. In the areas of my life where I have been sick for a long time, where I have almost stopped hoping, where I have built a little life around the brokenness and forgotten how to want what I once wanted, I say yes to Him today. Yes, Lord, I want to be made well. I stop rehearsing the obstacles. I stop explaining why the healing has not happened. I lift my eyes to the Healer standing in front of me. Speak the word today, Jesus. I will rise. I will take up my bed. I will walk. In Jesus’ name. Amen.

Declaration

I say yes to Jesus’ healing question today. I stop rehearsing the obstacles. I lift my eyes to the Healer. He speaks the word, and I rise, take up my bed, and walk.
